newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit falls to 2.5098 a dollar as US funds sell.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit falls to 2.5098 a dollar as US funds sell.

text.p: The ringgit skidded against the U.S. dollar on selling led by U.S. funds and on the back of the surge of the dollar/yen rate, dealers said.
Around 0755 GMT, ringgit was quoted at 2.5083/93 a dollar, after falling as low as 2.5098 earlier. It closed in Kuala Lumpur trading on Monday at 2.4965/75.
The rise of the Singapore dollar against the ringgit also depressed the Malaysian currency, the dealers said.
Research house I.D.E.A. said a U.S. hedge fund was believed to be behind the selling via a few investment houses, with an amount believed to total $200 million.

"Sources also told us that the recent ringgit selling was related to a large U.S. hedge fund liquidating their long three-month outright position (established in January 1997) which will mature over the coming week," it said.
Added a dealer at a large Malaysian bank: "(The U.S. funds) say the best situation now is to pull out especially as the U.S. is more promising -- interest rates are higher and likely to increase."
At 2.5098, the ringgit is at its lowest level in three months, since falling to 2.4970 on January 6.
The Malaysian central bank has not intervened so far to support the ringgit. Dealers speculated that Bank Negara would probably only intervene if the ringgit edges lower to 2.51.

In Malaysia's basket of trade currencies, the strength of the dollar is balanced by the weakness of the yen and should therefore be quite neutral on its export-competitiveness, one market analyst said.
The dollar was propelled to a fresh four-year high against the yen in Tokyo, at 126.12.
At 0800 GMT, the ringgit was also at 1.7413/32 per Singapore dollar, down from 1.7254/73 on Monday.
